meta_description: The Pied Piper story and moral, the original Hamelin legend, and read-aloud tips that teach children the importance of keeping a promise. A classic tale guide for ages 5–7.

content.text:
What kind of story is The Pied Piper?

The Pied Piper is the tale of a man who drove out a town's swarms of rats with the mysterious sound of his flute — a legend-like story that teaches just how important it is to keep a promise.

content.alt: The Pied Piper - The original Pied Piper story
content.text:
The original Pied Piper story

It is a legend from the German town of Hamelin, made widely known after the Brothers Grimm recorded it. Its heart is the ending in which the town, having promised a reward if the rats were cleared away, breaks its promise, and the piper plays his flute once more and leaves. It's a story about the price of not keeping one's word.

content.alt: The Pied Piper - A summary of the Pied Piper story
content.text:
A summary of the Pied Piper story

A town plagued by swarms of rats promises the Pied Piper a reward and asks him to drive the rats away. The piper leads all the rats out with the sound of his flute, but when the town fails to give the promised reward, he is deeply disappointed. (Tangobook's version reshapes this into a warm ending in which the town repents of its wrongdoing and keeps its promise.)

content.alt: The Pied Piper - The moral of The Pied Piper
content.text:
The moral of The Pied Piper

The heart of it is that a promise must always be kept, and breaking it costs you people's trust. Talk with your child about, "What happens when you don't keep a promise?" and share the value of trust together.
content.caption: Trust regained

content.alt: The Pied Piper - How to read it aloud to your child
content.text:
How to read it aloud to your child

Hum the sound of the flute — "tootle-loo~" — to give it a mysterious feel. Point out the consequences with, "What happened to the town that broke its promise?" and then carry it into an activity where your family sets a small promise of your own and keeps it. Best suited for ages 5–7.
content.caption: Practicing keeping a promise

content.text:
Frequently Asked Questions (FAQ)

Q. What age is The Pied Piper good for?
A. It's best suited for ages 5–7. It's a good time for children to understand themes like promises and trust.

Q. Is the Hamelin legend a true story?
A. It's an old legend from Hamelin, Germany. Some say it's connected to a real historical event, but it has been passed down as an adapted fairy tale.

Q. What kinds of conversations are good to have?
A. Talk together about "the importance of keeping a promise" and "what happens when a promise is broken."
